## 4. S-G-002 — pixel programs that read per-vertex attributes / compute their own barycentrics (P0/P10/P20) -> dx.op.attributeAtVertex

- owner / chain / hop: shared / shader / 5 MSC 4.0.3 (back/src/msc)
- freq: 4,852 (census:2026-11-27); used=yes; status=gap
- Xbox hardware / driver does: RDNA2 interpolates in LDS: a pixel program can read P0/P10/P20 (parameter at each vertex) and compute any interpolation (flat, provoking vertex, custom)
- deviation: MSC 4.0.3 refuses dx.op.attributeAtVertex.f32 (MSC manual: "GetAttributeAtVertex not supported"; 4852 of 12067 Ps containers = 40%; 330 CREATE_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE refusals in the 370 s run). Every pipeline with such a pixel shader is not created, its draws are dropped: the largest single block of missing geometry/materials seen in the run. (Another hand is working on this in metal-livetr.) Run r6: 330 refusals, 103 pipelines, 102 mesh (C-B-011).
- restore_plan (how to break through): Four routes under investigation: MSC switch / Metal-native per-vertex fragment inputs / DXIL rewrite before MSC / translator switch; fidelity first (the lead's list, 2026-11-27). One candidate for the translator route: SV_Barycentrics (accepted, linear only, MSC manual) plus the three vertex values as plain inputs supplied per-vertex from the vertex/mesh stage (flat-pull via a vertex-pulling stage-in buffer indexed by SV_PrimitiveID*3+vertex) and manual interpolation in the pixel shader. Fidelity: exact for linear interpolation; perspective-correct weights come from SV_Barycentrics (perspective) and centroid is refused by MSC (feature table). Feasibility 可行 for non-centroid; 待验证 for centroid/sample modes. Sources: MSC UserManual.md "Feature support matrix" (metal-irconverter 4.0.3), 2026-11-27; census/mac-side.md.
- tests: —
- notes: code: emit/lower.rs per_vertex; census.json failures; mac-side.md. Same cause 330x in the run.

## 7. mac.loader.masked_default_off — masked-store patch NOT applied by default: needs tracking ON under Rosetta (stores_need_patching) or VICTORY_PATCH_MASKED set

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / loader patch L1 gating (apps/victory/src/mac.rs, masked::choice)
- freq: 1,234 (static-census); used=yes; status=gap
- Xbox hardware / driver does: n/a
- deviation: CONFIRMS the reported suspicion for the product code: with Rosetta and fault tracking off (the default) choice(None, needed=false) is None, so 0 of 1234 masked stores are patched; the log line "patched" in the runs appears only because tools/mac/run.sh (line 48) and the integration runlt.sh export VICTORY_PATCH_MASKED=all (the first sets it even with tracking off; runs new-10..new-18 show tracking off and 1234 patched). A bare launch (tools/macos/victory.sh, a direct wine victory.exe) patches nothing; if anything then turns tracking on (VICTORY_FAULT_TRACKING=1), the extra BUILD_1_0_2_1_EXTRA RVAs (8 plain 256-bit sites of #144) are only added when VICTORY_PATCH_MASKED is unset, so under run.sh (=all) they are NOT patched.
- restore_plan (how to break through): Make the decision explicit and logged: patch whenever Rosetta (cost: 1234 jumps, no runtime cost when no fault); apply the 8 extra RVAs together with "all"; add a unit test for plan() covering the 4 combinations. Wide patch L2 is likewise never on by default (VICTORY_PATCH_WIDE unset in every script).
- tests: masked::patch_tests::stores_are_patched_by_default_only_when_needed (decision only); no test for mac.rs plan/apply
- notes: Why it matters: the title writes through masked stores into memory that any later tracking would guard; unpatched = fatal only if a guard fault hits one (probe), so with tracking off the exposure is when the title itself touches unmapped/protected memory.

## 8. shared.rt.bvh_build — dispatches of the title's ray-tracing structure builder (XboxBvhBuilder.dll, 53 compute pipelines: unpack of shipped static BVHs, build/refit of dynamic ones, CopyForBVHUpdate): dropped unless VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=1 and all builder pipelines have host pipelines (pipeline.rs:351 builder_runs; draw.rs:3150 dispatch)

- owner / chain / hop: shared / command / shared D3D12.X -> host D3D12 (before seam A)
- freq: 1,168 (log:logs/run-2026-11-27b/b3-diag-stacks/stderr.log:20045-37719 (8 five-second windows 14:07:09-14:08:01Z, 667-1712 dispatches/frame, mean 1168; reason 'a stage of the ray-tracing structure builder, which is off'); research/world-drops/20261127-2301/cold/stderr.log:4127-9153 (129-1475)); used=yes; status=gap
- Xbox hardware / driver does: the console GPU builder library builds and refits the BVH (64-byte AMD nodes) on the GPU every frame; static world structures ship packed and are unpacked in place by builder programs (DecompressHeader, Box32/Box16Rehydration, LeafRehydration)
- deviation: default OFF on every launcher (tools/mac/run.sh, tools/macos/victory.sh, tools/metal/run.sh set no RT variable). Every builder stage is dropped (counted in 'dropped ... without a host pipeline'): no dynamic BVH is built, no static BVH rehydrated; trace programs find nothing (docs/fork-ray-tracing.md:140 'every ray misses'). Deliberate, 3 legitimate reasons: (1) all-or-none safety: a partly running builder wrote garbage bounds into title memory and killed the title (pipeline.rs:255-281, run 98); (2) cost ~40 ms/frame on 7900XTX (fork doc:3-7); (3) open correctness gaps: dynamic structures overlap (8/65 good in light-10, 48/275 in light-15, doc:109-117), a replay capture with the builder on hangs the card (doc:126). Cold cache + BUILDER=1 passed the title's 30 s GPU watchdog (ec648b34 message; fix not in mac/livetr).
- restore_plan (how to break through): 1) one run of mac/livetr with VICTORY_BVH_BUILDER=1 VICTORY_BVH_QUARANTINE=1 to read 'stays off ... which=[hashes]' or 'runs' (0.5 d + a game run, needs the user's go); 2) port ec648b34 (builder pipelines queued at creation, not made on the recording thread) from refs/remotes/win-all/gpu/cf-lamp2px (0.5 d); 3) first-lane scan programs: no offline blocker on the new base (52/52 translate and build), so only the run in step 1 can show otherwise (0 d, was 1-5 d); 4) title memory by address (memory.rs) on D3DMetal under Wine+Rosetta (3-6 d, unknown); 5) lift quarantine, compare structures with a CPU build by bvh.rs node rules (3-5 d). Total 7-12 person-days (the report's 8-17 counted 1-5 d for step 3). Queue position: after the world geometry is drawn (mesh/GS host gaps dominate the visible loss). Fidelity path = run the title's own builder + traversal, not the Metal RT API.
- tests: none (no unit test of builder_runs / is_builder gating in mac/livetr)
- notes: Gate introduced by fxceless 578d459c (commit date 2026-11-24), kept by the user's Windows line (scripts/play.ps1:26, only with -RayTracing). On the OLD base (origin/main, upstream #481/#2118) the builder was ON whenever all its pipelines were made (pipeline/builder.rs, no switch): different semantics, do not mix. Offline state on the new base (census 2026-11-27, host wave 32, translator of this tree): the 52 unique XboxBvhBuilder.dll containers translate 52/52 and make 52/52 Metal pipelines (victory-census convert --kind cs --isolate --only, 0 aborts); 10 of them are wave64, among them the 3 first-lane scan programs (src offsets 0x99160, 0x9a830, 0x9be80), which translate WITHOUT VICTORY_FIRSTLANE_OWN=1 (the same 52/52 with it; the shortcut only changes 2 unrelated containers). The title creates 53 pipelines: the 53rd is not a distinct container here.

## 16. mac.loader.clwb_nop — clwb write-back loops replaced by NOPs (only if exactly 8 loops are found)

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / loader patch L4 (clwb.rs)
- freq: 8 (log); used=yes; status=unproven
- Xbox hardware / driver does: CLWB pushes dirty lines to memory so non-coherent consumers (GPU, DMA) see CPU writes.
- deviation: Write-back dropped. Safe on this path because all title memory is read by our own CPU code (copies for the GPU: unified memory, CPU-coherent). Would break if the GPU read title memory without a CPU copy (zero-copy) and CPU caches were not coherent.
- restore_plan (how to break through): Today: keep NOP. If zero-copy is ever built (mach_vm_remap / MTLBuffer no-copy on the title pages), replace by a real flush: clflush is available under Rosetta (probe) or rely on Apple silicon CPU/GPU coherency for shared memory (Apple docs: unified memory; 待核实 for explicit cache maintenance on shared MTLBuffers).
- tests: victory-loader mac::clwb tests::finds_the_loops_the_title_has_and_only_those (native)
- notes: A test would need a runtime check that no GPU read bypasses the CPU: add counter "title pages read by GPU without copy" (0 today).

- deviation: Wine returns an invalid-info-class status: placeholder() is never true, so memory that is a placeholder is not recognised (only matters with VICTORY_FAULT_TRACKING=1).
- restore_plan (how to break through): High fidelity and cheap: our own registry knows every placeholder we create (xmem.rs placeholder branch), answer from it instead of asking the kernel; or carry a 20-line Wine patch (tools/macos/patches/) adding class 7 to ntdll/unix/virtual.c.
- tests: watch::many_askers_tests::holes_are_known_until_the_runtime_tells, watch::many_askers_tests::no_mapping_is_lost_between_askers, watch::tests::what_is_left_alone_is_no_known_hole (3 FAIL under Wine)
- notes: Only reached with tracking on; frequency unknown.

## 50. mac.fault.xmem_no_write_watch — MEM_WRITE_WATCH left off the pools under Rosetta

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / victory-hle xmem.rs (A6)
- freq: not measured (unknown); used=yes; status=unproven
- Xbox hardware / driver does: GPU reads memory directly.
- deviation: No kernel write-watch: written pages unknown, so whole copies (same cost as tracking off). Wine emulates write watch with page protection, which hits Rosetta unresumable faults.
- restore_plan (how to break through): With tracking restored, turn on again; test: pool alloc has/hasn't MEM_WRITE_WATCH per mode.
- tests: none specific (xmem tests do not assert it)
- notes: —

## 51. mac.hle.commit_quota — commit-limit assumption: title budget (title_limit) from console::title_memory vs host commit

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / victory-hle xmem.rs commit(), commit_refused(); Wine/macOS commit
- freq: not measured (unknown); used=yes; status=unproven
- Xbox hardware / driver does: Console OS enforces a 13.5 GB title budget and fails commits past it.
- deviation: Our budget is a number we give the title; the host does not enforce it, so over-commit is not refused (and swap/compression may stall) instead of failing as on Xbox.
- restore_plan (how to break through): Account title commits in the HLE (sum of committed MEM_COMMIT) and refuse past the console budget, as the Xbox OS does; test with a title-like allocation sequence.
- tests: xmem::tests::commit_limit_report_includes_request_and_system_commit, transfers_shrink_the_title_budget, statistics_have_the_console_layout
- notes: 16 reservations total 62 GB virtual; only committed part matters.

## 52. mac.hle.cool_fox_residency — 32 GB residency budgets, fallback heaps, GPU pool back-off and deferred uploads under low commit

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / victory-gpu residency.rs (cool_fox 32 GB residency budgets), pool.rs back-off
- freq: not measured (unknown); used=yes; status=unproven
- Xbox hardware / driver does: Xbox has unified GDDR6 with no residency management.
- deviation: D3DMetal does not implement MakeResident (stub), so residency control is a no-op on that host; budgets assume a PC GPU with separate VRAM. Back-off branch unexercised.
- restore_plan (how to break through): On the Metal backend use MTLResidencySet (Metal 3+/4; 待核实 for macOS 27) to implement the budget for real; on D3DMetal nothing can be done. Add a forced-commit-limit test (VICTORY env) to exercise the back-off.
- tests: residency::tests (bake_and_lookahead_leave_room_for_live_game_allocations, either_constraint_enters_pressure_and_both_must_recover, prefetch_respects_existing_budgets_and_resumes_after_recovery); pool::tests::a_failed_block_is_not_retried_for_each_small_upload (Wine: pass)
- notes: Mac observation only; the budgets were written on Windows PCs.

## 53. mac.hle.zero_copy_alias — zero-copy title buffers via mach_vm_remap (copy=FALSE) onto D3DMetal buffer pages

- owner / chain / hop: mac / command / Mac fork #204 alias.rs NOT ported (PATCHES.md "Not ported")
- freq: not measured (unknown); used=yes; status=gap
- Xbox hardware / driver does: Title memory IS the GPU memory.
- deviation: In mac/livetr there is NO zero-copy: every buffer the GPU needs is shadowed and copied (shadow.rs), copy-back after writes. The title's GPU writes into its memory are landed by copying (land.rs), not shared.
- restore_plan (how to break through): Port alias.rs (x86_64 raw mach_msg2_trap path, D3DMetal only) as a Mac-gated module; or on the native Metal backend map title pages with newBufferWithBytesNoCopy (page-aligned, 待核实 constraint with Wine mappings). Cost: mach MIG traps from Rosetta, EXC_GUARD on macOS 27 for mach_msg_trap (alias.rs comment).
- tests: none in this tree (alias.rs absent)
- notes: Fidelity: removes the copy latency/race window; correctness impact today unknown (copies hold).
